stem: A 33-year-old female undergoes surgical repair of a muscle avulsion involving the lateral surface of the ilium. The disrupted muscle originates between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines and inserts on the greater trochanter. Which of the following movements would most directly be weakened by loss of this muscle's function?
explanation: Gluteus minimus originates between anterior and inferior gluteal lines and abducts and medially rotates the hip.
optionFeedback: Gluteus maximus chiefly extends and laterally rotates the hip.
Adductor magnus contributes to adduction and extension.
Gluteus minimus originates between anterior and inferior gluteal lines and abducts and medially rotates the hip.
Biceps femoris flexes and laterally rotates the knee.

distractors.A: Gluteus maximus chiefly extends and laterally rotates the hip.
distractors.B: Adductor magnus contributes to adduction and extension.
distractors.D: Biceps femoris flexes and laterally rotates the knee.

stem: A 48-year-old male undergoes pelvic surgery requiring exposure of the ischial spine. During the operation, a ligament extending from the sacrum to this bony prominence is identified. Together with the sacrotuberous ligament, it contributes to the formation of the sciatic foramina. Which of the following ligaments is being described?
explanation: The sacrospinous ligament runs from sacrum to ischial spine and helps convert sciatic notches into foramina.
optionFeedback: The sacrospinous ligament runs from sacrum to ischial spine and helps convert sciatic notches into foramina.
The ischiofemoral ligament reinforces the posterior hip capsule.
The iliolumbar ligament connects the lower lumbar spine to ilium.
The pubofemoral ligament reinforces the anteroinferior hip capsule.

distractors.B: The ischiofemoral ligament reinforces the posterior hip capsule.
distractors.C: The iliolumbar ligament connects the lower lumbar spine to ilium.
distractors.D: The pubofemoral ligament reinforces the anteroinferior hip capsule.

stem: A 22-year-old dancer develops severe proximal posterior thigh pain while performing a split. MRI demonstrates injury to a proximal hamstring tendon following excessive lengthening during simultaneous hip flexion and knee extension. The affected muscle inserts on the posterior aspect of the medial tibial condyle. Which of the following muscles is most likely injured?
explanation: Semimembranosus inserts on the posterior medial tibial condyle and is commonly injured with excessive hamstring lengthening.
optionFeedback: The short head inserts on fibular head and does not cross the hip.
Gracilis begins at the pubis and inserts at pes anserinus.
Semitendinosus inserts at pes anserinus, not posterior medial condyle.
Semimembranosus inserts on the posterior medial tibial condyle and is commonly injured with excessive hamstring lengthening.

distractors.A: The short head inserts on fibular head and does not cross the hip.
distractors.B: Gracilis begins at the pubis and inserts at pes anserinus.
distractors.C: Semitendinosus inserts at pes anserinus, not posterior medial condyle.

stem: A patient sustains a selective injury to the common fibular division of the sciatic nerve within the proximal posterior thigh. The tibial division remains intact. Which of the following posterior thigh muscles would be most directly affected by this injury?
explanation: The short head of biceps femoris is the posterior thigh exception supplied by the common fibular division.
optionFeedback: Semimembranosus receives tibial division innervation.
The short head of biceps femoris is the posterior thigh exception supplied by the common fibular division.
Semitendinosus receives tibial division innervation.
The long head receives tibial division innervation.

distractors.A: Semimembranosus receives tibial division innervation.
distractors.C: Semitendinosus receives tibial division innervation.
distractors.D: The long head receives tibial division innervation.

stem: A 45-year-old female undergoes decompression of the deep gluteal space. The surgeon identifies a small nerve supplying a rectangular muscle extending from the ischial tuberosity to the intertrochanteric crest. Which of the following additional muscles receives innervation from this nerve?
explanation: The nerve to quadratus femoris also supplies inferior gemellus.
optionFeedback: Superior gemellus receives the nerve to obturator internus.
Obturator internus receives its own eponymous nerve.
The nerve to quadratus femoris also supplies inferior gemellus.
Piriformis receives direct branches from the sacral plexus.

distractors.A: Superior gemellus receives the nerve to obturator internus.
distractors.B: Obturator internus receives its own eponymous nerve.
distractors.D: Piriformis receives direct branches from the sacral plexus.

stem: A 58-year-old male undergoes excision of a tumor involving the lateral aspect of the proximal femur. Postoperatively, imaging demonstrates disruption of the gluteus maximus insertion on the femur, although the iliotibial tract remains intact. Which of the following bony structures represents the damaged muscular attachment?
explanation: Deep fibers of gluteus maximus insert on the gluteal tuberosity; other fibers join the iliotibial tract.
optionFeedback: Quadratus femoris inserts near the quadrate tubercle.
The trochanteric fossa receives obturator externus.
Iliopsoas inserts on the lesser trochanter.
Deep fibers of gluteus maximus insert on the gluteal tuberosity; other fibers join the iliotibial tract.

distractors.A: Quadratus femoris inserts near the quadrate tubercle.
distractors.B: The trochanteric fossa receives obturator externus.
distractors.C: Iliopsoas inserts on the lesser trochanter.

stem: During examination of a patient with a suspected gluteal nerve injury, a physician evaluates the function of the tensor fasciae latae. The patient demonstrates weakness of hip flexion, abduction, and medial rotation. Which of the following structures receives the distal attachment of this muscle through the iliotibial tract?
explanation: The iliotibial tract inserts on Gerdy's tubercle at the lateral tibial condyle.
optionFeedback: The iliotibial tract inserts on Gerdy's tubercle at the lateral tibial condyle.
The medial femoral condyle is not the insertion of the tract.
Biceps femoris attaches principally to fibular head.
The patellar ligament inserts at tibial tuberosity.

distractors.B: The medial femoral condyle is not the insertion of the tract.
distractors.C: Biceps femoris attaches principally to fibular head.
distractors.D: The patellar ligament inserts at tibial tuberosity.

stem: A 62-year-old female presents with localized numbness over the superior aspect of the buttock following lumbar surgery. Motor function of the gluteal muscles is preserved. The injured sensory branches are derived from the posterior rami of the upper lumbar spinal nerves. Which of the following nerves are most likely affected?
explanation: Superior cluneal nerves originate primarily from upper lumbar posterior rami and supply superior buttock skin.
optionFeedback: Inferior cluneal nerves arise from posterior femoral cutaneous branches.
Middle cluneal nerves arise from sacral posterior rami.
Superior cluneal nerves originate primarily from upper lumbar posterior rami and supply superior buttock skin.
Superior gluteal nerve primarily supplies gluteal abductor muscles.

distractors.A: Inferior cluneal nerves arise from posterior femoral cutaneous branches.
distractors.B: Middle cluneal nerves arise from sacral posterior rami.
distractors.D: Superior gluteal nerve primarily supplies gluteal abductor muscles.

stem: A 31-year-old male sustains a penetrating wound to the inferior gluteal region. Neurologic examination demonstrates severe weakness of knee flexion, ankle dorsiflexion, and plantarflexion. Sensory loss affects most of the leg and foot, although sensation along the medial leg remains intact. Which of the following nerves is most likely injured?
explanation: Sciatic injury affects hamstrings and both tibial and common fibular distributions; saphenous sensation medially is spared.
optionFeedback: Femoral injury primarily impairs knee extension and medial leg sensation.
Sciatic injury affects hamstrings and both tibial and common fibular distributions; saphenous sensation medially is spared.
Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve is sensory to posterior thigh rather than motor to leg.
Inferior gluteal injury impairs gluteus maximus.

distractors.A: Femoral injury primarily impairs knee extension and medial leg sensation.
distractors.C: Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve is sensory to posterior thigh rather than motor to leg.
distractors.D: Inferior gluteal injury impairs gluteus maximus.

stem: A physician prepares to administer an intramuscular injection in the gluteal region of an adult patient. The anterior superior iliac spine and iliac crest are used as landmarks to identify an appropriate injection site. Which of the following locations minimizes the risk of injuring the major neurovascular structures of the deep gluteal region?
options: Immediately superficial to the ischial tuberosity
Directly over the greater sciatic foramen
explanation: The superolateral/ventrogluteal region identified with bony landmarks avoids the main deep gluteal neurovascular structures.
optionFeedback: Inferomedial placement risks the sciatic nerve and deep vessels.
The ischial tuberosity is close to the proximal hamstrings and sciatic nerve.
The greater sciatic foramen transmits major neurovascular structures.
The superolateral/ventrogluteal region identified with bony landmarks avoids the main deep gluteal neurovascular structures.

distractors.A: Inferomedial placement risks the sciatic nerve and deep vessels.
distractors.B: The ischial tuberosity is close to the proximal hamstrings and sciatic nerve.
distractors.C: The greater sciatic foramen transmits major neurovascular structures.

stem: A 29-year-old male sustains a localized tendon injury near the superolateral boundary of the popliteal fossa. Physical examination demonstrates weakened flexion and lateral rotation of the knee. Which of the following muscle tendons is most likely involved?
explanation: Biceps femoris forms the superolateral boundary and laterally rotates the flexed knee.
optionFeedback: Semimembranosus forms the superomedial boundary and medially rotates the flexed knee.
Medial gastrocnemius forms the inferomedial boundary.
Biceps femoris forms the superolateral boundary and laterally rotates the flexed knee.
Semitendinosus forms the superomedial boundary and medially rotates the flexed knee.

distractors.A: Semimembranosus forms the superomedial boundary and medially rotates the flexed knee.
distractors.B: Medial gastrocnemius forms the inferomedial boundary.
distractors.D: Semitendinosus forms the superomedial boundary and medially rotates the flexed knee.

stem: A surgeon approaches the popliteal fossa to remove a small benign mass. During dissection, the superior medial boundary of the fossa is identified by tracing two adjacent hamstring tendons. Which of the following muscles form this boundary?
options: Long and short heads of biceps femoris
Medial and lateral heads of gastrocnemius
explanation: Semitendinosus and semimembranosus form the superomedial boundary.
optionFeedback: Semitendinosus and semimembranosus form the superomedial boundary.
Biceps femoris forms the superolateral boundary.
Sartorius and gracilis are pes anserinus contributors, not the paired hamstring boundary.
The gastrocnemius heads form the inferior boundaries.

distractors.B: Biceps femoris forms the superolateral boundary.
distractors.C: Sartorius and gracilis are pes anserinus contributors, not the paired hamstring boundary.
distractors.D: The gastrocnemius heads form the inferior boundaries.

stem: A 70-year-old male is found to have an aneurysm of the popliteal artery. During vascular surgery, collateral blood flow around the knee is evaluated before the affected segment is excluded from the circulation. Which of the following vascular networks is most directly responsible for providing alternative pathways around the knee joint?
options: Cruciate anastomosis of the proximal thigh
explanation: Genicular branches and contributions from neighboring arteries form a collateral network around the knee.
optionFeedback: The plantar arch supplies the sole.
The trochanteric network supplies the proximal hip region.
The cruciate anastomosis is in the proximal posterior thigh.
Genicular branches and contributions from neighboring arteries form a collateral network around the knee.

distractors.A: The plantar arch supplies the sole.
distractors.B: The trochanteric network supplies the proximal hip region.
distractors.C: The cruciate anastomosis is in the proximal posterior thigh.

stem: A patient undergoing surgery in the gluteal region sustains an injury to a neurovascular bundle emerging through the greater sciatic foramen inferior to the piriformis muscle. Postoperatively, he has pronounced weakness when attempting to rise from a seated position, while his ability to maintain a level pelvis during single-leg stance is preserved. Which of the following vessels most closely accompanies the injured nerve?
explanation: The inferior gluteal artery accompanies the inferior gluteal nerve, which innervates gluteus maximus for powerful extension.
optionFeedback: The superior bundle exits above piriformis and supplies abductors.
The inferior gluteal artery accompanies the inferior gluteal nerve, which innervates gluteus maximus for powerful extension.
Obturator artery passes toward the obturator canal.
Medial circumflex femoral artery courses around proximal femur rather than accompanying the inferior gluteal nerve.

distractors.A: The superior bundle exits above piriformis and supplies abductors.
distractors.C: Obturator artery passes toward the obturator canal.
distractors.D: Medial circumflex femoral artery courses around proximal femur rather than accompanying the inferior gluteal nerve.

stem: A 51-year-old female presents with pelvic instability following injury to the superior gluteal nerve. During rehabilitation, she asks why her trunk shifts toward the affected side when bearing weight on that limb. Which of the following explanations best describes the biomechanical purpose of this compensatory movement?
options: It increases the moment arm of body weight around the affected hip.
It increases the muscular demand placed on the weakened hip abductors.
It shifts the body's center of mass toward the affected hip, reducing the required abductor moment.
It transfers the primary function of pelvic stabilization to the knee flexors.
explanation: Leaning toward the affected stance hip reduces the gravitational adduction moment that weakened abductors must oppose.
optionFeedback: A stance-side lean shortens rather than lengthens the body-weight moment arm.
Shortening the moment arm reduces required abductor torque.
Leaning toward the affected stance hip reduces the gravitational adduction moment that weakened abductors must oppose.
Knee flexors do not replace hip abductor stabilization.

distractors.A: A stance-side lean shortens rather than lengthens the body-weight moment arm.
distractors.B: Shortening the moment arm reduces required abductor torque.
distractors.D: Knee flexors do not replace hip abductor stabilization.

stem: A 39-year-old male experiences persistent deep buttock pain following a traumatic injury. MRI demonstrates damage to a small muscle inserting on the quadrate tubercle of the intertrochanteric crest. Which of the following muscles corresponds to this anatomical attachment?
explanation: Quadratus femoris inserts at the quadrate tubercle and adjacent intertrochanteric crest.
optionFeedback: Obturator internus inserts on the medial surface of the greater trochanter.
Inferior gemellus joins the obturator internus tendon.
Piriformis attaches near the superior border of the greater trochanter.
Quadratus femoris inserts at the quadrate tubercle and adjacent intertrochanteric crest.

distractors.A: Obturator internus inserts on the medial surface of the greater trochanter.
distractors.B: Inferior gemellus joins the obturator internus tendon.
distractors.C: Piriformis attaches near the superior border of the greater trochanter.

stem: A patient undergoes a surgical procedure near the lesser sciatic foramen. The surgeon protects both the pudendal nerve and a vessel accompanying it around the ischial spine. Which of the following arteries follows this course to enter and supply the perineal region?
explanation: Internal pudendal vessels exit the greater sciatic foramen and reenter through the lesser sciatic foramen with the pudendal nerve.
optionFeedback: Internal pudendal vessels exit the greater sciatic foramen and reenter through the lesser sciatic foramen with the pudendal nerve.
Superior gluteal artery exits above piriformis and supplies gluteal tissues.
Inferior epigastric artery ascends the anterior abdominal wall.
Deep femoral artery supplies the thigh.

distractors.B: Superior gluteal artery exits above piriformis and supplies gluteal tissues.
distractors.C: Inferior epigastric artery ascends the anterior abdominal wall.
distractors.D: Deep femoral artery supplies the thigh.

stem: A 24-year-old athlete develops posterior thigh pain after sustaining a partial hamstring tear. Examination demonstrates weakness of knee flexion, hip extension, and medial rotation of the flexed knee. Imaging confirms injury near the posterior medial tibial condyle rather than the pes anserinus. Which of the following distal muscular attachments is most likely affected?
explanation: Semimembranosus attaches posteriorly on the medial tibial condyle and performs the described actions.
optionFeedback: Sartorius inserts at pes anserinus and flexes the hip.
Semimembranosus attaches posteriorly on the medial tibial condyle and performs the described actions.
Biceps femoris attaches to the fibular head and laterally rotates the flexed knee.
Semitendinosus inserts at pes anserinus.

distractors.A: Sartorius inserts at pes anserinus and flexes the hip.
distractors.C: Biceps femoris attaches to the fibular head and laterally rotates the flexed knee.
distractors.D: Semitendinosus inserts at pes anserinus.

stem: During a lumbar puncture, a physician palpates the superior border of each iliac crest to estimate the level of the lumbar vertebral column. A horizontal line connecting the highest points of these bony landmarks is used as a surface anatomical reference. Which of the following vertebral levels is most closely associated with this line in the lecture?
explanation: The lecture associates the intercristal line with L4; actual levels vary and can approximate the L4–L5 interspace.
optionFeedback: L1 is typically well superior to the intercristal line.
T12 is at the thoracolumbar junction, superior to the crests.
The lecture associates the intercristal line with L4; actual levels vary and can approximate the L4–L5 interspace.
S2 is below the usual intercristal line.

distractors.A: L1 is typically well superior to the intercristal line.
distractors.B: T12 is at the thoracolumbar junction, superior to the crests.
distractors.D: S2 is below the usual intercristal line.

stem: A 66-year-old male undergoes surgical excision of a lesion located along the lateral margin of the popliteal fossa. The surgeon identifies a nerve following the medial border of the biceps femoris tendon before continuing toward the fibular head. Which of the following nerves is being identified?
explanation: Common fibular nerve follows the lateral fossa near biceps femoris toward the fibular neck.
optionFeedback: Saphenous nerve runs along the medial lower limb.
Tibial nerve descends centrally through the popliteal fossa.
Medial sural cutaneous nerve arises from tibial nerve and descends posteriorly.
Common fibular nerve follows the lateral fossa near biceps femoris toward the fibular neck.

distractors.A: Saphenous nerve runs along the medial lower limb.
distractors.B: Tibial nerve descends centrally through the popliteal fossa.
distractors.C: Medial sural cutaneous nerve arises from tibial nerve and descends posteriorly.

stem: A 41-year-old male sustains an injury to the anterior compartment of the leg. During surgical exploration, a damaged artery is identified alongside the deep fibular nerve. The vessel normally originates from the popliteal artery and enters this compartment through an opening in the superior interosseous membrane. Which of the following vessels is injured?
explanation: Anterior tibial artery crosses the interosseous membrane to supply anterior compartment with the deep fibular nerve.
optionFeedback: Fibular artery primarily courses in the deep posterior compartment.
Anterior tibial artery crosses the interosseous membrane to supply anterior compartment with the deep fibular nerve.
Posterior tibial artery remains in the posterior leg.
Medial plantar artery arises distally from posterior tibial artery.

distractors.A: Fibular artery primarily courses in the deep posterior compartment.
distractors.C: Posterior tibial artery remains in the posterior leg.
distractors.D: Medial plantar artery arises distally from posterior tibial artery.

stem: A 28-year-old female sustains a fracture involving the base of the fifth metatarsal after suddenly inverting her foot while running. Radiographs reveal a small avulsed bone fragment at the distal attachment site of an evertor tendon. Which of the following muscles most likely exerted traction on this fragment?
explanation: Fibularis brevis inserts at the fifth metatarsal tuberosity and can avulse a fragment during inversion.
optionFeedback: Fibularis longus inserts at the medial cuneiform and first metatarsal base.
Tibialis anterior inserts on the medial foot.
Flexor digiti minimi brevis acts at the fifth proximal phalanx and is not the evertor tendon described.
Fibularis brevis inserts at the fifth metatarsal tuberosity and can avulse a fragment during inversion.

distractors.A: Fibularis longus inserts at the medial cuneiform and first metatarsal base.
distractors.B: Tibialis anterior inserts on the medial foot.
distractors.C: Flexor digiti minimi brevis acts at the fifth proximal phalanx and is not the evertor tendon described.

stem: A 38-year-old male undergoes surgical repair of a tendon laceration in the deep posterior compartment of the leg. Following the injury, he demonstrates weakness of flexion at the interphalangeal joint of the great toe, particularly during the push-off phase of walking. Which of the following muscles is most likely affected?
explanation: Flexor hallucis longus crosses the great toe IP joint and inserts on its distal phalanx, assisting push-off.
optionFeedback: Flexor hallucis longus crosses the great toe IP joint and inserts on its distal phalanx, assisting push-off.
Flexor hallucis brevis acts primarily at the MTP joint.
Flexor digitorum longus flexes digits 2–5.
Adductor hallucis primarily adducts the great toe.

distractors.B: Flexor hallucis brevis acts primarily at the MTP joint.
distractors.C: Flexor digitorum longus flexes digits 2–5.
distractors.D: Adductor hallucis primarily adducts the great toe.

stem: A 56-year-old female presents with progressive medial ankle discomfort and weakness during resisted inversion of the foot. MRI demonstrates injury to a tendon passing posterior to the medial malleolus and inserting primarily onto the navicular. Which of the following muscles is most likely involved?
explanation: Tibialis posterior passes behind medial malleolus, attaches prominently to navicular, and inverts and supports the medial arch.
optionFeedback: Tibialis anterior crosses the anterior ankle and inserts at medial cuneiform/first metatarsal.
Fibularis longus passes behind the lateral malleolus and everts the foot.
Tibialis posterior passes behind medial malleolus, attaches prominently to navicular, and inverts and supports the medial arch.
Extensor hallucis longus crosses anterior ankle and extends hallux.

distractors.A: Tibialis anterior crosses the anterior ankle and inserts at medial cuneiform/first metatarsal.
distractors.B: Fibularis longus passes behind the lateral malleolus and everts the foot.
distractors.D: Extensor hallucis longus crosses anterior ankle and extends hallux.

stem: A patient undergoes surgery requiring exposure of the structures within the tarsal tunnel. The surgeon identifies the tendons of tibialis posterior and flexor digitorum longus immediately posterior to the medial malleolus. Which of the following structures lies between the posterior tibial artery and the flexor hallucis longus tendon within this tunnel?
explanation: From anterior to posterior, the tunnel contains tibialis posterior, FDL, posterior tibial vessels, tibial nerve, and FHL.
optionFeedback: Deep fibular nerve courses anteriorly, outside the tarsal tunnel.
From anterior to posterior, the tunnel contains tibialis posterior, FDL, posterior tibial vessels, tibial nerve, and FHL.
Sural nerve courses around lateral ankle.
Great saphenous vein passes anterior to medial malleolus superficially.

distractors.A: Deep fibular nerve courses anteriorly, outside the tarsal tunnel.
distractors.C: Sural nerve courses around lateral ankle.
distractors.D: Great saphenous vein passes anterior to medial malleolus superficially.

stem: A 67-year-old male with peripheral arterial disease undergoes examination of the arterial pulses of the lower extremities. The physician palpates the region immediately posterior to the medial malleolus to evaluate perfusion through a major artery supplying the plantar foot. Which of the following vessels is being assessed?
explanation: Posterior tibial artery is palpable behind the medial malleolus and divides into plantar arteries.
optionFeedback: Dorsalis pedis is palpable on the dorsal foot.
Anterior tibial artery passes anterior to the ankle.
Arcuate artery courses across the dorsal metatarsal bases.
Posterior tibial artery is palpable behind the medial malleolus and divides into plantar arteries.

distractors.A: Dorsalis pedis is palpable on the dorsal foot.
distractors.B: Anterior tibial artery passes anterior to the ankle.
distractors.C: Arcuate artery courses across the dorsal metatarsal bases.

stem: A patient sustains a localized nerve injury near the lateral aspect of the ankle. Sensory examination reveals diminished sensation along the lateral border of the foot and posterolateral aspect of the distal leg. Strength testing demonstrates no significant motor deficits. Which of the following nerves is most likely injured?
explanation: Sural nerve is cutaneous to the posterolateral distal leg and lateral foot.
optionFeedback: Sural nerve is cutaneous to the posterolateral distal leg and lateral foot.
Deep fibular nerve supplies first dorsal web-space sensation and motor branches.
Medial plantar nerve supplies medial sole and selected intrinsic muscles.
Saphenous nerve supplies medial leg and foot skin.

distractors.B: Deep fibular nerve supplies first dorsal web-space sensation and motor branches.
distractors.C: Medial plantar nerve supplies medial sole and selected intrinsic muscles.
distractors.D: Saphenous nerve supplies medial leg and foot skin.

stem: A 55-year-old male undergoes surgical stripping of a superficial vein that passes posterior to the lateral malleolus and ascends along the posterior aspect of the calf. The surgeon traces the vessel proximally to its usual termination. Which of the following veins normally receives this superficial vessel?
explanation: Small saphenous vein usually drains into popliteal vein behind knee.
optionFeedback: The great saphenous vein typically terminates in femoral vein.
The usual termination of small saphenous is not the great saphenous, though variation exists.
Small saphenous vein usually drains into popliteal vein behind knee.
External iliac vein is proximal to inguinal ligament.

distractors.A: The great saphenous vein typically terminates in femoral vein.
distractors.B: The usual termination of small saphenous is not the great saphenous, though variation exists.
distractors.D: External iliac vein is proximal to inguinal ligament.

stem: A 35-year-old female sustains a penetrating injury involving the medial plantar nerve. Motor examination reveals difficulty abducting her great toe and flexing the proximal phalanges of several toes. Which of the following additional intrinsic foot muscles would most likely lose its innervation?
explanation: Medial plantar nerve supplies first lumbrical, abductor hallucis, FDB and typically FHB.
optionFeedback: Quadratus plantae receives lateral plantar innervation.
Medial plantar nerve supplies first lumbrical, abductor hallucis, FDB and typically FHB.
Adductor hallucis receives the deep branch of lateral plantar nerve.
Dorsal interossei receive lateral plantar innervation.

distractors.A: Quadratus plantae receives lateral plantar innervation.
distractors.C: Adductor hallucis receives the deep branch of lateral plantar nerve.
distractors.D: Dorsal interossei receive lateral plantar innervation.

stem: A 42-year-old male sustains an injury involving a muscle located in the second layer of the plantar foot. The affected muscle normally assists flexor digitorum longus by modifying the direction of traction exerted on its tendons. Which of the following muscles has most likely been injured?
explanation: Quadratus plantae inserts on the FDL tendon and helps redirect its oblique pull.
optionFeedback: FDB is a first-layer toe flexor with its own tendons.
Abductor digiti minimi is a first-layer muscle acting on fifth toe.
FHB is a third-layer great toe flexor.
Quadratus plantae inserts on the FDL tendon and helps redirect its oblique pull.

distractors.A: FDB is a first-layer toe flexor with its own tendons.
distractors.B: Abductor digiti minimi is a first-layer muscle acting on fifth toe.
distractors.C: FHB is a third-layer great toe flexor.

stem: During a neurologic examination, a physician asks a patient to spread the toes apart against resistance. The patient demonstrates weakness involving abduction of the second through fourth digits. Which of the following intrinsic muscle groups is primarily responsible for the impaired movement?
explanation: Dorsal interossei abduct digits 2–4 relative to the second digit.
optionFeedback: Plantar interossei adduct toes 3–5.
Lumbricals flex MTP and extend IP joints.
Dorsal interossei abduct digits 2–4 relative to the second digit.
FDB flexes digits 2–5 rather than abducting them.

distractors.A: Plantar interossei adduct toes 3–5.
distractors.B: Lumbricals flex MTP and extend IP joints.
distractors.D: FDB flexes digits 2–5 rather than abducting them.

stem: A 30-year-old female sustains a localized nerve injury affecting the deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve. Examination demonstrates weakness of great toe adduction, which may also impair muscular support of the transverse arch. Which of the following muscles is directly responsible for these functions?
explanation: Adductor hallucis adducts the hallux and helps maintain transverse arch; it receives deep lateral plantar innervation.
optionFeedback: Adductor hallucis adducts the hallux and helps maintain transverse arch; it receives deep lateral plantar innervation.
Abductor hallucis abducts the hallux and receives medial plantar innervation.
FHL flexes the hallux and receives tibial innervation in the leg.
EHB extends the hallux and receives deep fibular innervation.

distractors.B: Abductor hallucis abducts the hallux and receives medial plantar innervation.
distractors.C: FHL flexes the hallux and receives tibial innervation in the leg.
distractors.D: EHB extends the hallux and receives deep fibular innervation.

stem: A patient sustains an injury to the intrinsic musculature of the plantar foot. When asked to flex the metatarsophalangeal joints while extending the interphalangeal joints of the lateral four digits, the patient demonstrates significant weakness. Which of the following muscle groups normally contributes most directly to this combined movement?
explanation: Lumbricals flex MTP joints and extend IP joints of digits 2–5 via extensor expansions.
optionFeedback: Fibularis muscles act principally at the ankle and foot rather than this toe movement.
Long flexors flex IP joints rather than extend them.
Long extensors extend toes rather than flex MTP joints.
Lumbricals flex MTP joints and extend IP joints of digits 2–5 via extensor expansions.

distractors.A: Fibularis muscles act principally at the ankle and foot rather than this toe movement.
distractors.B: Long flexors flex IP joints rather than extend them.
distractors.C: Long extensors extend toes rather than flex MTP joints.

stem: A 26-year-old male sustains a laceration across the dorsum of his foot. The injury damages a small muscle originating from the calcaneus and inserting onto the proximal phalanx of the great toe. Which of the following muscles is most likely affected?
explanation: EHB originates on calcaneus and inserts on base of proximal hallux phalanx.
optionFeedback: EHL originates in the leg and inserts on distal phalanx.
EHB originates on calcaneus and inserts on base of proximal hallux phalanx.
FHB is plantar and flexes the MTP joint.
Abductor hallucis is plantar and abducts the hallux.

distractors.A: EHL originates in the leg and inserts on distal phalanx.

stem: A 58-year-old female presents with numbness over the medial aspect of her leg and foot following harvest of the great saphenous vein. explanation: Saphenous nerve is a sensory femoral branch accompanying great saphenous vein in the medial leg.

stem: A 20-year-old long-distance runner presents with exercise-induced pain along the posteromedial border of the tibia after increasing her training mileage. explanation: Medial tibial stress syndrome commonly produces diffuse posteromedial tibial pain related to repetitive loading.
optionFeedback: Tarsal tunnel causes plantar paresthesias and medial ankle symptoms.

stem: A 47-year-old male sustains an ankle injury that disrupts the tendon of a superficial posterior leg muscle. The affected muscle originates from the femoral condyles and crosses both the knee and ankle joints. Which of the following muscles is most likely involved?

stem: A 63-year-old patient with diabetes mellitus develops a deep plantar ulcer.
